Candidate 40 passes as supplied. The artwork maps confidently to the labeled routing: Hole 1 is the upper lakeside par 5, Hole 2 is the winding return toward the lower-center green, and Hole 3 is the dry par 3 to the right-side green. It preserves the substantial lake extents, playable fairway corridors, and greenside bunker relationships. The 5:3 landscape shows a compact irregular shared property, folded routing, grassy breaks between selective groves, continuous interior grass, and putting surfaces rendered as single natural greens with restrained fringes.

Hole 1 offers a credible safer route away from the long right-side lake and a more aggressive chance to reach in two; the landing corridor remains usable. Hole 2's dogleg and fairway water create a meaningful line choice, with room to play conservatively. Hole 3 provides a dry, bunker-guarded long-par-3 contrast, with a generous safe-options count supporting playability. The par-5/4/3 sequence and different hazard emphasis give strong within-round variety. Reachable par 5s and doglegs recur in recent rounds, but this combination, sequence, and dry par 3 provide sufficient novelty. Simulation results are supportive rather than conclusive, and the previews show credible landing space. No clear, safely correctable geometry mismatch warrants an edit.
